title: How a Red Light Knows You're Waiting 🚦 #shorts
description:
Those thin lines cut into the road at intersections hide a loop of wire. A roadside box runs alternating current through it, and when your car's metal rolls over the loop, eddy currents weaken its magnetic field, so the signal knows you're there. Here's why bikes sometimes get missed, and where to stop so the light sees you.

Follow Hidden Mechanics for more everyday engineering, explained in under a minute.
